body.statement:
Let \(p\in(0,1)\) be fixed. If \(X_1,X_2,\ldots\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) random variables and \(K_m=\sum_{a=1}^mX_a\), then
\[
 \frac{K_m-mp}{\sqrt{mp(1-p)}}\Rightarrow N(0,1)
 \qquad\text{as }m\to\infty.
\]

source.locator: Section 2, pp. 102--103, normal approximation for a binomial proportion
source.verbatim_statement: In introductory statistics texts and courses, the confidence interval CI_S is usually presented along with some heuristic justification based on the central limit theorem.

attestation.note: Verified against Brown, Cai, and DasGupta (2001), Statistical Science 16(2), author/JSTOR PDF mirror https://web.pdx.edu/~ihd/stat563.S17/brown.pdf, Section 2 p.103; nearby text defines p-hat=X/n and the binomial standard error and calls this the Wald large-sample normal test.
